method: KML and GeoJSON both list a position as longitude first, then latitude, with an optional altitude third, so nothing is reordered here: the conversion rewrites structure. Reading KML, the XML is parsed first, including comments, CDATA sections, the five predefined entities and numeric character references, and the root must be a kml element. Every Placemark in document order becomes a GeoJSON Feature: a name child becomes properties.name with whitespace collapsed, a description child becomes properties.description, and each ExtendedData Data or SchemaData SimpleData value becomes a string property under its name attribute. A Point, LineString, Polygon, MultiGeometry or LinearRing child inside a Placemark becomes the geometry; a MultiGeometry whose members all share one type becomes MultiPoint, MultiLineString or MultiPolygon, a mixture becomes a GeometryCollection and a single member is unwrapped. A LinearRing outside a Polygon has no GeoJSON form, so it becomes a closed LineString, and a ring whose first and last positions differ has its first position repeated at the end to make a valid GeoJSON ring; each of these is reported as a warning. A placemark with no geometry is kept with a null geometry, and a placemark holding only gx:Track, gx:MultiTrack or Model gets a null geometry and a warning. Writing KML, a Feature becomes a Placemark, name and description properties become elements, other string, number and boolean properties become ExtendedData Data values, non-scalar properties are left out with a warning, a null geometry becomes an empty Placemark, and GeometryCollection or any Multi type becomes MultiGeometry. Coordinates must hold two or three finite numbers, with longitude within -180 to 180 and latitude within -90 to 90; a KML Point must hold exactly one position, a LineString or GeoJSON line at least two, and a polygon ring at least four with the first and last positions equal - KML rings that are not closed are closed here, while a GeoJSON ring that is not closed is refused. Numbers are printed in JavaScript's shortest exact form, so coordinates keep the precision pasted. Folders, styles, styleUrl, time stamps, regions, NetworkLink, GroundOverlay, ScreenOverlay and Model are not geometry and are dropped, and a description that contains KML markup has its tags dropped and its text kept, with a warning. Input is limited to 2 MB of text, everything runs in the browser with no upload, storage or network access, and the page does not render the map.
